keywords.def: A number that can be written as a/b, where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
The distance of a number from 0. It is never negative.

en.text: A rational number is a/b with b not zero. You can place it on a number line, find its absolute value, compare and order it, and add, subtract, multiply and divide with sign rules. You also used rational numbers for sharing and interest.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A number that can be written as a/b, where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
The distance of a number from 0. It is never negative.

screens.title: Sign rules: match each rule to its result
screens.why:
Adding two negatives: the sizes add, the sign stays −. So negative.
Multiplying two negatives: same signs give +. So positive.
Positive ÷ negative: different signs give −. So negative.
a + (−a): a number plus its opposite is 0.

screens.ask: Add fractions and a whole number: 3/4 + 9/7 + 2 = ___
Multiply a mixed number by a fraction: 2 3/7 × 1/4 = ___
screens.why:
Change: 2 3/7 = (2 × 7 + 3)/7 = 17/7.
Multiply the tops: 17 × 1 = 17.
Multiply the bottoms: 7 × 4 = 28.
Answer: 17/28.

Different signs: the answer is negative.
Flip −5/2 to −2/5: 3/4 × (−2/5) = −6/20.
Divide top and bottom by 2: −3/10.

screens.text: Spot the mistake: Lidya says −2/3 ÷ 4/9 = −8/27. What went wrong?
opts: She multiplied instead of dividing. The answer is −3/2.
Only the sign is wrong. The answer is 8/27.
screens.ans: She multiplied instead of dividing. The answer is −3/2.
screens.why:
−2/3 × 4/9 = −8/27, so Lidya multiplied.
To divide, flip the divisor: 4/9 → 9/4.
−2/3 × 9/4 = −18/12.
Divide by 6: −3/2. The sign − was right; the method was wrong.
screens.clue: Work it out yourself: flip the divisor and multiply.

items.text: Compare negative fractions: true or false? −5/3 > −8/11
items.why:
−5/3 = −1 2/3 ≈ −1.67.
−8/11 ≈ −0.73.
−1.67 is further left than −0.73, so −5/3 < −8/11.
The statement is false.

items.text: Compare three numbers: true or false? 3 5/7 > 23/7 > 19/6

items.why:
The inside, x − 5, is 4 or −4.
x − 5 = 4 gives x = 9.
x − 5 = −4 gives x = 1.
Check: |9 − 5| = 4 and |1 − 5| = |−4| = 4.

Place a negative fraction: tap where −3/4 goes.
items.why:
−3/4 is negative, so it is left of 0.
3/4 is proper, so it is between −1 and 0.
Split 0 to −1 into 4 equal parts.
Count 3 marks left of 0.

items.text: Classify a number: what is the smallest set containing −7?
items.why:
−7 is negative, so it is not in ℕ or W.
It has no fraction part, so it is an integer.
The smallest set is ℤ.

items.why:
x is 6 units from 0.
Right of 0: 6. Left of 0: −6.

items.title: Order the numbers in ascending order (smallest first)
items.why:
Change to decimals: −1/2 = −0.5 and 2/3 ≈ 0.67.
Negatives: −1.5 is further left than −0.5.
Positives: 0.67 < 1.2.
Order: −1.5, −1/2, 2/3, 1.2.

LCM of 3 and 4 is 12: −2/3 = −8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12.
Different signs: 9 > 8, so the sign is +.
9 − 8 = 1.
Answer: 1/12.

Different signs: the product is negative.
Sizes: 3 × 10 = 30 and 5 × 9 = 45.
30/45: divide by 15 to get 2/3.
Answer: −2/3.

Different signs: the quotient is negative.
Flip 7/4 to 4/7: 7/8 × 4/7 = 28/56.
28/56 = 1/2.
Answer: −1/2.

test.text: Rational numbers: which is NOT a rational number?
test.why:
0/5 = 0, −5 = −5/1 and 0.5 = 1/2 are rational.
5/0 has denominator 0.
Dividing by 0 is not allowed.
So 5/0 is not rational.

test.text: Opposites: true or false? The sum of two opposite numbers is 0.
test.why:
Opposites are a and −a.
a + (−a) = 0.
Example: 3/4 + (−3/4) = 0.
True.

Same signs: the product is positive.
Sizes: 1 × 1 = 1 and 2 × 2 = 4.
Answer: 1/4.

test.text: Number sets: which statement is false?
opts: Every rational number is an integer
test.ans: Every rational number is an integer
test.why:
Every integer n = n/1 is rational: true.
0 is a whole number: true. −3/4 is rational: true.
But 1/2 is rational and not an integer.
So "Every rational number is an integer" is false.

Brackets first: LCM of 3 and 2 is 6.
−2/3 + 1/2 = −4/6 + 3/6 = −1/6.
Then −1/6 × 6 = −6/6 = −1.
Answer: −1.
